QUESTION:
Using the provided dataframe containing (i) multiple dataset membership indicator columns (0/1) for MLO participant sets and membrane-bound organelle control sets, (ii) a fixed non-PS negative/background set (e.g., hNoPS-test), and (iii) multiple predictor score columns (e.g., PLAAC, PScore, catGRANULE, SaPS-8fea/10fea, PdPS-8fea/10fea), evaluate and compare screening performance across datasets. Determine whether predictors perform consistently better on MLO participant datasets than on membrane-bound organelle controls.

ANSWER:

Yes. All seven phase-separation (PS) predictors evaluated — PScore, PLAAC, catGRANULE, SaPS-8fea, PdPS-8fea, SaPS-10fea, and PdPS-10fea — perform consistently and substantially better on MLO (membraneless organelle) participant datasets than on the membrane-bound organelle control (mitochondrial proteomics). The performance gap is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney U, p = 1.49 × 10⁻⁷) and practically meaningful across every predictor and every dataset.

KEY NUMBERS:
• Mean ROC-AUC across all predictors and all four MLO datasets: 0.742 (range: 0.651–0.895 per dataset, 0.665–0.811 per predictor).
• Mean ROC-AUC for the mitochondrial proteome control: 0.411. No predictor exceeds AUC = 0.5 on the membrane-bound control.
• ΔAUC (MLO − Membrane): 0.331 overall. Per-predictor Δ ranges from +0.208 (PScore) to +0.455 (PdPS-10fea).
• 28/28 predictor × MLO-dataset combinations yield AUC > 0.5. 0/7 predictor × membrane combinations yield AUC > 0.5.
• Cohen's d (standardized mean difference vs hNoPS background): mean +1.28 for MLO datasets (large effect); mean −0.07 for mitochondrial (negligible).

PER-DATASET RANKING (mean AUC across all predictors):
1. PhaSepDB high-throughput (MLO):     0.895 — strongest signal; all PhaSepDB positives were in predictor training sets (training-removed AUC unavailable)
2. G3BP1 proximity labeling (MLO):     0.771 — robust even after training-set removal (drops to 0.597, still above membrane)
3. DACT1-particulate proteome (MLO):   0.653 — moderate, with SaPS-10fea reaching 0.801
4. OpenCell nuclear punctae (MLO):     0.651 — moderate, with PdPS-8fea reaching 0.725
5. Amyloid fiber-forming proteins:     0.596 — intermediate (amyloid shares sequence features with PS)
6. Mitochondrial proteomics (membrane): 0.411 — consistently below random; mitochondrial proteins are anti-correlated with PS scores

BEST PREDICTORS:
PhaSePred 10-feature classifiers (PdPS-10fea, SaPS-10fea) show the largest MLO-membrane gap (Δ = 0.45–0.46), followed by the 8-feature versions. The single-feature predictors (PScore, PLAAC, catGRANULE) show smaller but still positive gaps (Δ = 0.21–0.23).

EFFECT OF TRAINING-SET REMOVAL:
After removing proteins present in predictor training sets, PhaSepDB loses all positives (65 proteins), confirming training-set contamination. The remaining MLO datasets retain an AUC advantage over mitochondrial (mean MLO AUC drops from 0.691 to 0.596; mitochondrial unchanged at 0.411). The gap persists, confirming that the MLO advantage is not solely an artifact of training-set overlap.

CONCLUSION:
PS predictors discriminate MLO participant proteins from a non-PS background far better than they discriminate membrane-bound organelle proteins from the same background. This is consistent with the biophysical expectation that MLO participants are enriched in phase-separation-driving sequence features (disorder-promoting residues, aromatic stickers, charge patterning), whereas mitochondrial proteins are folded, globular, and compositionally similar to the non-PS proteome background.
